route.body: 4xx and 5xx errors are wrapped as {"error":{"code":<number>,"message":"<string>"}}. A missing bearer token answers 400 {"message":"No bearer token"}. An invalid token answers 401 {"message":"Authentication error"}. An invalid cursor answers 500 (observed) with {"errors":[{"message":"<string>"}]}. These status codes and shapes are observed; the API reference documents only selected 4xx and 500 responses.

v2.body: { type, retryable, errors: [ { code, message, parameter } ] } with HTTP status derived from the error type
v2.retry_signal: retryable flag in the response body; always false for Object Query errors

Translate v2 filter keys to the public OQ field names as documented in the filter and sort translation reference, section subscriptions-versions. Key mapping: id→Id, account_id→AccountId, contract_effective→ContractEffectiveDate, invoice_owner_account_id→InvoiceOwnerId, updated_time→UpdatedDate, subscription_number→Name, state→Status, start_date→TermStartDate, latest_version→IsLatestVersion, version→Version, end_date→TermEndDate. Field names are case-insensitive. Translate state enum values: draft→Draft, pending_activation→Pending Activation, pending_acceptance→Pending Acceptance, active→Active, expired→Expired, canceled→Cancelled, paused→Suspended. Identifier fields (id, account_id, invoice_owner_account_id) accept 32-character hexadecimal record IDs. Date fields (contract_effective, start_date, end_date) use YYYY-MM-DD. Timestamp fields (updated_time) use ISO 8601 format.

Translate the v2 sort key to the public OQ field name using the same key mapping table as filter[] (see the filter and sort translation reference, section subscriptions-versions). Pass exactly one sort[] value; the value is the public field name followed by .asc or .desc. Default sort when no sort[] is supplied: version.desc. Field names are case-insensitive.

Rename page_size to pageSize. The public pageSize parameter accepts 1 to 99 (default 10), the same range as v2 page_size. A value from 1 to 99 is passed through unchanged; a literal outside 1 to 99 is clamped to the nearest bound in the migrated code (the public route rejects it with HTTP 400, as v2 does) and the change is reported. Pass the nextPage value returned by the previous page unchanged as the cursor query parameter; only use cursors issued by this operation; an absent or null nextPage means there is no further page.

For each row of `data[]` in the successful JSON response, build the `custom_fields` object. Build the object only when the row contains `customFields`: a missing or null `customFields` leaves `custom_fields` out of the result (the `__c` properties are then not used). Subscription versions follow the subscription rule. Use the `customFields` array when the row has one, otherwise the `custom_fields` array; turn each `{key, value, type}` entry into `key: value` (when a key appears more than once, the last entry wins). Then convert `long` and `number` values to numbers, convert `boolean` values to true or false, and leave other types unchanged; null values stay null. If the row has neither array, collect every property whose name ends in `__c` into the object; an empty array gives `{}` and the `__c` properties are then not used. Include `custom_fields` only when it was requested.

unsupported.note: The public APIs do not accept this header. The v2 API accepted the x-custom-auth and zuora-cache-enabled request headers; neither header has a public equivalent. The subscription versions route did not wire a cache handler, so zuora-cache-enabled had no effect on this operation. The public APIs authenticate via a bearer token in the Authorization header and optionally accept zuora-entity-ids to scope the request to an entity and zuora-track-id for request tracing. Send the OAuth bearer token in the Authorization header. Pass zuora-entity-ids to scope the request to a specific entity, or zuora-track-id for request tracing. Do not send zuora-cache-enabled; the public APIs have no such header. No vetted GraphQL example is available.
